chunks: When Jesus perceived their unbelief, he asked: 'Who will help me in the way of God?' The disciples said: 'We are the helpers of God. We believe in God; and You be our witness that we submit.'
ai.seo_question: Who were the Hawariyyun (disciples) and what did they say to Jesus when he asked for helpers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'al-Hawariyyun' (the Disciples) is often linked to the concept of pure, unwavering support for divine truth, with some traditions identifying them as the progenitors of the Imams' followers. This verse highlights the transition from Jesus' earthly ministry to the establishment of a committed community, emphasizing their declaration of 'Islam' (submission) as a universal monotheistic stance rather than a later sectarian identity. The narrative underscores the continuity of prophetic mission, where the disciples' affirmation serves as a precursor to the broader acceptance of God's will by the faithful.
